criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: The report explains the reef-monitoring purpose, identifies scientific and conservation users, and gives a strong Australian rationale. The mission function and intended benefits are understandable, with relevant sources. However, it does not define a specific payload, measurable objectives, or operational requirements, so the concept is not yet complete enough for Accomplished.

evidence.quote: Hundreds of millions of humans rely on reefs for food, natural protection, jobs, and tourism.
would allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict and react to coral bleaching events.

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: A week-by-week Gantt chart is accompanied by descriptions of research, launch, orbit, ground control, communications, end-of-life, and STK work. A useful source list is included and the tasks appear feasible within the stated timeline. The plan lacks contingency provision, detailed deliverables or dependencies, and a clear explanation of why particular activities or sequencing suit this mission.

evidence.quote: The goal is to brainstorm and research as many possible strategies for the satellite’s launch/orbit

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: Relevant background research and STK tutorials show some work has been completed. However, the submission presents no preliminary technical design results, calculations, simulations, or interpretation. This fits minor progress rather than a good preliminary set of results.

evidence.quote: researched into how coral bleaching occurs and its severity

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: The report has a clear section structure, a readable and labelled Gantt chart, and relevant sources are linked to numbered citations. The prose is generally understandable, but includes awkward or informal phrasing, and the references are mostly bare URLs without full bibliographic details. The chart also does not explain the meaning of its grey cells.

technical_issues.issue: The text links ocean acidification to coral bleaching too directly. Marine heat stress is the main proximate cause of mass bleaching; acidification is a separate stressor that can impair coral calcification. The 30% figure is better described as an increase in hydrogen-ion concentration, not a general increase in ocean acidity.

Near-real-time monitoring is asserted without specifying the sensor, revisit interval, latency, or communications design. If the concept relies on one low-Earth-orbit satellite, it would not provide continuous or near-real-time coverage of the reef; the requirement needs a coverage analysis or a multi-satellite/other architecture.

No technical mission parameters or preliminary results are provided, such as a candidate orbit, coverage/revisit estimate, payload capability, or link analysis. The plan names these future tasks but does not yet demonstrate their feasibility.

overall: Weighted result: 58/100 (using the criterion weights and marks out of 10). The mission rationale and project schedule are credible, but the report is light on defined requirements and contains no preliminary engineering results. Clarify the bleaching science and establish coverage and payload requirements to guide the full design.

feedback.summary: You present a clear Australian reef-monitoring rationale, identify relevant users, and provide a credible project schedule and useful sources. To reach the next rubric level, make the mission requirements measurable, build in contingency planning, and show preliminary engineering results that test whether the mission can meet its coverage and monitoring goals.
next_steps: In “Mission Concept & Rationale,” define a candidate sensor and measurable objectives, including coverage, revisit interval, and data latency. Clarify that marine heat stress is the main proximate cause of mass bleaching, while acidification is a separate stressor, and describe the 30% figure as an increase in hydrogen-ion concentration.

Develop Image 1 into a mission-specific plan with deliverables, task dependencies, and contingency time. Explain why the sequence suits this mission, and provide full bibliographic details for the sources listed under “Useful Links.”

Add preliminary engineering evidence in “Project Plan & Preliminary Progress,” such as a candidate orbit, coverage or revisit estimate, payload capability, or communications analysis. Interpret what the results show about feasibility, and improve the chart legend and informal phrasing.

criteria.C1: You clearly explain the reef-monitoring purpose, Australian relevance, and scientific and conservation users. To reach Accomplished, define a specific payload, measurable objectives, and operational requirements; also distinguish the roles of heat stress and acidification in bleaching.
criteria.C2: Image 1 gives a readable week-by-week schedule, and “Useful Links” identifies relevant sources. To reach Accomplished, add mission-specific deliverables, dependencies, and contingencies, and explain why the schedule and its sequencing fit the mission.
criteria.C3: Your background research and completed STK tutorials show initial progress. To reach Accomplished, include and interpret preliminary engineering results—such as an orbit, coverage/revisit estimate, payload capability, or link analysis—to demonstrate feasibility.
criteria.C4: Your report has clear sections, a labelled Gantt chart, and numbered citations linked to relevant sources. To reach Accomplished, refine informal or awkward wording, provide complete reference details, and explain the meaning of the grey cells in Image 1.
